drivers: AI and chip stocks are bouncing after last week's biggest weekly drop for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq since June, when worries about higher rates and how the AI build-out will be financed hit data-center operators hardest: Nasdaq-100 futures +1.3%, S&P 500 futures +0.5%, Dow futures −0.2%. Semis lead (SOXX +3.6% pre-market; Intel +4% on a JPMorgan upgrade, Micron, Sandisk, AMD and Broadcom +3–4%), and neoclouds rebound with CoreWeave +6% on a Goldman upgrade. Oil eased (WTI ~$98, Brent ~$108) after President Trump waived some Russia sanctions, though Strait of Hormuz shipping attacks continue, and the 10-year yield is steady near 5.10%. Europe is weaker (DAX and FTSE −1.2–1.3%) while China's Q3 GDP grew 4.5% y/y; Hong Kong was closed. Earnings week ahead includes SpaceX (Tue after the close), Tesla and Meta (Wed), plus Netflix, GM, IBM and AT&T; today Cleveland-Cliffs jumped ~14% on Q3 results and Fifth Third reported.
